audit.why: Heavily Qiyana-favoured (60.86% WR, 327 games): ASol is a stack-scaling immobile mage with one escape; Qiyana wins every laning stage and must strangle his scaling — page frames it this way and the packet chart is Qiyana on all seven rows.

Spikes: levels 3-5 (all elements, all-in through his weak early game), 6 (burst beats his telegraphed R), first item (stealth one-shot), late (his critical-stack teamfighting is the only threat). All four spikes[] present.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated/wrong names: spikes[1] called his R 'Falling Star / Voice of Light' (Voice of Light does not exist on current ASol; R is Falling Star / The Skies Descend) and called Astral Flight his E (it is W; Singularity is E). whys[4] and wants.foe[2] repeated 'Voice of Light'. spikes[2], whys[5] and late referenced 'passive shielding' — his passive is Stardust, there is no shield in his kit. Cooldowns field had no digit. Full chart rows 3-5 said Skill and row 6 said Aurelion Sol against content/packet Qiyana x7. The Singularity execute/resist-bypass interaction was missing.
audit.why: Kit authority: W Astral Flight 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s, E Singularity 12s with center execute and percent-health damage, R 120/110/100s stun, Q is an interruptible channel your CC cancels.
audit.corrected: Names fixed to Falling Star and Astral Flight (W), shield claims replaced with Stardust, real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns including the Singularity execute warning, chart sides aligned to Qiyana x7 with rewritten whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes.
audit.corrected: New bodies: CC breaking his Q channel, and the W-swap-as-kill-fuel rule.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Terrashape (element swap) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight (W): 22s at rank 1, 16s max — his only escape; he is a stationary battery while it is down. - Singularity (E) runs 12s and its center executes low HP — never limp through it. - Your 120s ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather.
edits.after: Ice-Q roots him mid Breath of Light — the channel breaks on any CC, so a root both stops the damage and starts your string.

edits.before: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: W spent on poke leaves you elementless when Astral Flight is finally down — the swap is the kill window's fuel.

edits.before: Element-cycle the trades: E-ice-Q roots, auto, rock-Q the execute line. The lane is a terrain quiz.
edits.after: You close every gap and freeze to choke his stack economy — he has nothing to interrupt your dash.

edits.before: Supreme Display online — any fight near a wall is a stun lottery you rigged. Hug terrain like rent depends on it.
edits.after: Level 6: his Falling Star stun is slow and telegraphed — sidestep the ring and your all-in still connects.

edits.before: First item spike: the full element string deletes squishies. Force the brush-line fights.
edits.after: First item: you one-shot him from brush stealth before his Stardust stacks can matter.

edits.before: Late Qiyana flanks through her own R: shockwave the objective wall, string the stunned, and vanish into grass.
edits.after: Still his 1v1 executioner — keep him too poor to ever reach the critical stacks his teamfighting needs.

edits.before: Level 6 his telegraphed Voice of Light does nothing to stop your gap-close and burst.
edits.after: Level 6 his telegraphed Falling Star does nothing to stop your gap-close and burst.

edits.before: First item you one-shot him from brush stealth before his shielding or stacks matter.
edits.after: First item you one-shot him from brush stealth before his Stardust stacks matter.

edits.before: His Falling Star / Voice of Light (R) is slow and telegraphed and does nothing to stop your gap-close. Sidestep the stun ring, slow him with Rock, and Supreme Display of Talent deletes him before he can even land the crash — engage the moment his Astral Flight (E) is on cooldown.
edits.after: His Falling Star (R) stun is slow and telegraphed and does nothing to stop your gap-close. Sidestep the stun ring, slow him with Rock, and Supreme Display of Talent deletes him before he can even land the crash — engage the moment his Astral Flight (W) is on cooldown.

edits.before: First-item you one-shot him from brush stealth: W in, E-Q slow, R burst evaporates him before his passive shielding or stacks matter. He has only one flight escape, so bait or ward it and he has zero outs against your combo.
edits.after: First-item you one-shot him from brush stealth: W in, E-Q slow, R burst evaporates him before his Stardust stacks matter. His only escape is Astral Flight — bait or track it and he has zero outs; just never limp through Singularity's center low.

edits.before: First-item and beyond you remain his executioner in the 1v1: from stealth you one-combo him before his shielding matters, ignoring his telegraphed ultimate entirely. He becomes a terrifying teamfighter at critical stacks, so the mandate is to keep him poor — pick him before fights and end the game on the massive lead your lane dominance builds.

edits.after: Land a Falling Star stun to peel your dive

notes: Suspect name confirmed against the kit: 'Voice of Light' is legacy ASol and appeared in three content fields — all fixed to Falling Star; spikes[1] also mislabeled Astral Flight as E (it is W, 22s->16s; Singularity is E, 12s). 'Passive shielding' claims removed — his passive is Stardust, no shield exists. Missing interactions (Singularity center execute / percent-health bypassing resists) now surfaced in breakdown.cooldowns and spikes[2]; the resist-bypass matters little to itemization for an AD assassin, so no item edit made. Chart: content and packet were Qiyana x7; full rows 3-6 aligned with rewritten whys, no win[N] edits (no-ops). Row ratings left as-is.
